newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece rejects EU mediation initiative with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Greece rejects EU mediation initiative with Turkey.

text.p: Greece on Thursday rejected a European Union-inspired proposal for mediation in its disputes with neighbouring Turkey and set its own conditions for a dialogue with Ankara.

"There is no substance in this proposal," Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos told a news conference after talks with Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country holds the rotating European Union presidency until June 30.
Pangalos was referring to a proposal by EU diplomats for each side to nominate independent mediators, known as "Wise Men", to negotiate their differences.
Turkey, which is not a member of the 15-nation bloc, said on Wednesday it was willing in principle to accept the EU initiative.
"We would be happy to do so if making use of methods like help from third parties were helpful for dialogue," Turkish foreign ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news conference.

Pangalos said a dialogue with Turkey would only be possible if Ankara denounced war threats against Greece, talks were opened on the accession of Cyprus in the EU and territorial differences were resolved through international courts.
Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller has said Turkey would go to war if Greece were to extend its territorial waters from six to 12 miles in the Aegean Sea separating the two countries.

"No country can threaten us with war," Pangalos said. "This threat must be removed if there is to be any rapproachement. At this point we are not willing to extend our waters although we have the right to do it (under international law)."

He said that scheduled talks for Cyprus to become an EU member should begin before the end of the Dutch presidency in June and that the internationally recognised Greek-Cypriot government in Nicosia should represent the island in the talks.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkish troops invaded and occupied its northern third after a coup attempt in Nicosia engineered by a military junta then ruling Greece.

A number of Greece's EU partners, including Germany and Britain, said in February that Cypriot accession would be politically and almost physically impossible without at least some progress between the island's Greek and Turkish communities.
"We have to find a way to satisfy the British government if it has the same position until June," Pangalos said.

He said that Van Mierlo would convey the Greek conditions to Ankara when he arrives later on Thursday and that Greece, a member of the European Union since 1981, would continue to block EU funds to Turkey.
NATO allies Greece and Turkey came close to war last year over an uninhabited islet in the eastern Aegean.
